title: CRISPRi/a screens in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes identify glycolytic activation as a druggable target for doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity
model: iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, hCRISPRi-v2 / hCRISPRa-v2 druggable-genome sublibraries
contrast: CRISPRi: doxorubicin vs vehicle, 72 h (2 vs 2); CRISPRa (secondary) the same
paper_method: Horlbeck et al. 2016 guide scoring (phenotype score and Mann-Whitney p); hits at score > 2 (CRISPRi) or > 1 (CRISPRa), p < 0.01
paper_calls: 21 CRISPRi and 43 CRISPRa protective genes; CRISPRi top 5 HPGDS, SCMH1, CA12, ERBB2, DGKH; CA12 validated
barcs_calls: CRISPRi: 1 gene at FDR 0.10 (IL2, a one-guide jackpot), 0 against the control null; CRISPRa: 1,020 depleted calls from guide blocks missing in the doxorubicin libraries, not interpretable, none enriched
named_hits: Rank among doxorubicin-enriched CRISPRi genes: CA12 #1 of 2,484 (FDR 0.35), ERBB2 #5, HPGDS #8, DGKH #178, SCMH1 #1,359; none at FDR 0.10
verdict: CA12 is BARCS's strongest credible CRISPRi gene, with HPGDS and ERBB2 in its top 8, but with two weakly selected replicates per arm nothing passes FDR 0.10. The CRISPRa doxorubicin libraries are missing blocks of guides, which makes its depletion calls technical.
